memos.risk:
Risk officer read: this is a refusal, not a sizing exercise.

Key facts: the coin is 30 minutes old and down 48.6% from its 30-minute high, with a last-15-minute return of -15.7% and net outflow of 56 SOL. Sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.91, and the curve shows a 53% bundle share, so the "ORGANIC" label doesn't hold up against the data. Pool depth of 257 SOL is thin against $1.04M of recent volume, so a $20 ticket plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip leaves little room for a 20-50% stop to execute cleanly.

Sizing if the desk were forced to buy: $5, stop at 20%, hold 15 minutes. But I recommend skipping. Refuse any size given the active distribution, the bundling, and the post-peak slide.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying is weak, and the brief mostly argues against it.

The strongest point: the coin is alive, with a large trading base. In the last 15 minutes, 4,611 buyers and about $1.04M of volume, and the first two minutes after graduation drew 408 non-agent buyers with a top-5 buyer share of only 15.6%. No airdrop dump, and the class is labeled ORGANIC.

But the recent tape is deteriorating. Net flow over 15 minutes is roughly flat (+56 SOL on $4,330 bought), the return is -15.7%, the price is 49% off its 30-minute high, and sellers (3,481) far outnumber the flow suggests a fading bid. Sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was 0.91, meaning early buyers were already exiting. Roughly 53% of curve volume came from bundled buys, which is a warning sign of manufactured activity. A 7x return over 30 minutes means much of the move is already spent.

I can't make a case that real demand will persist for the next 30-60 minutes. The best I can say is that the coin has organic-looking breadth and the pool is deep enough to exit. Against a base rate of roughly -20% for this kind of buy and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost, the desk should skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: this is a post-graduation coin that already ran +700% in 30 minutes and has since drawn down 49% from its high, with the last 15 minutes showing -15.7% and net flow of only +56 SOL on $1.04M volume. Sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.91 with 408 buyers, and the curve shows a 53% bundle share, so a large slice of early supply was bundled and is likely being distributed into retail buying now. Sellers (3,481) far outnumber the buyers' sell pressure would suggest, and a 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost means we need a sustained rebound just to break even. The brief gives no evidence of operator backing (no 500+ SOL concentrated buy), so the operator-backed break-even base rate doesn't apply. Organic label aside, the momentum has rolled over and insiders with bundled supply are the obvious exit liquidity source. Skip.
